clue.text: Well-heeled man's end comes in fateful fashion

indicators.note: the end of man's comes in, that is goes inside, the reworked letters
to fashion something is to shape it anew, so the letters of fateful are reworked
end points to the final letter of man's, its N

explanation.surface: A rich man meets his end in a way that feels decided by fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' makes AFFLUET from FATEFUL, and 'comes in' puts N, the end of man's, inside it before the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-heeled wears good shoes, an idiom for being wealthy and prosperous.

clue.text: The quartet travel north in baggage-wagon

parts.note: a quartet is a group of four
to travel is to go
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Four people head north in the luggage van of a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A fourgon is a French luggage van or baggage cart, borrowed into English.

clue.text: Observe court card is missing in this game

indicators.note: the court card is missing, so its letter drops out of the word for observe

parts.note: to observe is to look
K is the king, a court card in a pack

explanation.surface: A player notices that a picture card has gone missing from the pack.
explanation.walkthrough: Court cards are the king, queen and jack; K for king is the one taken from LOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Loo is an old card game, once popular for gambling in eighteenth-century Britain.

clue.text: Well-preserved dams, from an earlier civilisation?

definitions.text: Well-preserved dams, from an earlier civilisation?

parts.words: Well-preserved dams, from an earlier civilisation?
parts.note: dams are mothers of animals, so mothers kept intact through embalming by an ancient Nile people

explanation.surface: Ancient river barriers that have survived in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dams' suggests river barriers, but it means mothers, and 'Well-preserved' means embalmed, a pun on mothers and embalmed bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Embalmed bodies from the Nile kingdoms are called mummies, which is also a word for mothers.

clue.text: Label the French instrument

parts.note: a tab is a small tag or label
la is French for the (feminine)

explanation.surface: A request to put a name tag on a French musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The tabla is a pair of small Indian hand drums, a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Birds found Scotsman was different

parts.note: Mac is a stock informal name for a Scotsman

indicators.note: different means the letters of was are made to appear in another order

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers report that a Scot behaved unlike usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaws are large, brightly coloured parrots of tropical America.

clue.text: Horticultural trade replacing green dating mark

indicators.note: replacing means the letters of green dating mark are put back in new places

explanation.surface: A gardening business swaps the use-by label on its vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Market gardening is growing fruit and vegetables commercially to sell, a branch of horticulture.

clue.text: Link I sever, in America

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in America, a state of the USA

parts.note: to link is to connect
to sever is to cut

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a tie while living in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'in America' stands for one of the states in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Connecticut is one of the New England states of the USA.

clue.text: The outer garments affording protection from it?

indicators.note: the garments are outer, so their word wraps around the word the

parts.note: wear is clothing in general, as in menswear
taken as written

explanation.surface: Outer clothes are what keep you sheltered from the elements.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' that the outer garments protect from is the definition, read in the context of the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain, wind and cold are what outer clothing keeps off, so 'it' here is the elements.

clue.text: Ugly roundabout the English are first to praise

indicators.note: the English are first, so their letter leads the answer

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of ugly and round are turned about into a new order

parts.note: a round shape is an O

explanation.surface: Even an ugly person gets praised first by the English.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'roundabout' does two jobs, read as 'round' (a ring shape, O) and 'about' (the signal to turn the letters around); the original likely printed two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech or piece of writing in high praise of someone.

clue.text: Saloon ahead, to which I've taken almost all of the nobility

parts.note: a saloon is a bar, as in saloon bar
on means ahead, as in go on
I have, so the letter I takes the next piece

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of all is dropped

explanation.surface: A pub with a nobleman's bar, where someone has drunk nearly everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Baronial means belonging to barons, lords of the peerage.

clue.text: A dog called Hamlet?

parts.note: Shakespeare's prince of Denmark could be described as an important man from Denmark, which is also the name of a big dog breed

explanation.surface: A pet named after Shakespeare's prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet is prince of Denmark, so he is a notable Dane; the large dog breed shares the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a giant dog breed, and Hamlet is the most famous person from Denmark.

clue.text: Calculate on having to make a speech then spit it out!

parts.note: to calculate in the sense of reckon or suppose is to expect
to orate is to make a formal speech

explanation.surface: An orator is told to plan their address and then deliver it bluntly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spit it out' looks like an urge to speak plainly, but here it means literally spitting.
explanation.definitionFit: To expectorate is to cough up phlegm from the chest and spit.

clue.text: Parrot in the chop-suey

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the words the chop-suey

explanation.surface: A pet bird has got into the Chinese takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' is a verb here: to parrot is to repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo is to repeat words mindlessly, just as a mimicking bird does.

clue.text: Card game you may take on holiday

definitions.meaning: a children's card game where players call out on matching cards
a quick photograph taken while away

explanation.definitionFit: Snap is a matching card game, and a snap is a casual photograph.

clue.text: Gorilla sat uneasily, swamp predators appearing

indicators.note: uneasily signals the letters of gorilla sat are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A great ape sits nervously as dangerous creatures emerge from the marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Alligators are large reptiles that hunt in the swamps of the southern US and China.

clue.text: Display of birds here replacing elk

indicators.note: replacing means the three letters of elk are set back in a different order

explanation.surface: Birds put on a show where a deer used to graze.
explanation.definitionFit: A lek is the ground where male birds such as grouse gather to court females.

clue.text: He might have turned out a hunter

definitions.text: He might have turned out a hunter

parts.words: He might have turned out a hunter
parts.note: a hunter is also a pocket timepiece with a hinged cover, which a craftsman would turn out, that is produce

explanation.surface: Someone who could have grown up to be a huntsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' suggests became, but means manufactured, and a hunter is a pocket watch with a metal lid.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who makes timepieces would produce hunters, watches with protective lids.

clue.text: Item in a new collection — it's alive!

indicators.note: new signals the letters of item and the collection are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: ana is a collection of sayings or anecdotes

explanation.surface: An exhibit placed in a new museum collection suddenly comes to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collection' is a crossword convention: an ana is a published collection of a person's sayings or anecdotes. 'new' is the signal to rearrange; 'in a' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Animate as an adjective means living, having life.

clue.text: Strike by one hand

definitions.meaning: to hit someone, especially with an open hand
the end of a sleeve, found next to the hand

explanation.definitionFit: A cuff is a light blow, and also the band at a sleeve's end at the wrist.

clue.text: Increases strength by jogging if forty

definitions.note: the definition is a third-person verb phrase, while the answer is its base form

indicators.note: jogging shakes up the letters of if forty into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone in their forties takes up running to get fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To fortify is to make stronger, reinforcing a place or a person.

clue.text: Sunk teeth into first olive, getting oil from this fruit

parts.note: to have sunk teeth into something is to have bit it

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of olive

explanation.surface: Someone bites into an olive and extracts oil from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bito is an African and Asian tree whose fruit yields an oil.

clue.text: Hoping for an Oscar, doctor competes with Jack

definitions.note: the definition describes the person rather than naming them

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
to vie is to compete
jack tar is an old name for a sailor, also simply tar

explanation.surface: A physician rivals a man called Jack for an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a man's name, but Jack tar is a sailor, and tar alone means a sailor too.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen actor of fame hopes for an Academy Award, the film industry's top prize.

clue.text: Farewell to tip-top servant

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

indicators.note: top picks the topmost, first letter of tip

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye to a first-class manservant.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a personal manservant who looks after his employer's clothes.

clue.text: Spreading alarm — I, with a student will get fever of this type!

indicators.note: spreading alarm means its letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plates of a learner driver

explanation.surface: Panic spreads that a student has caught a tropical fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Malarial describes the recurring fever caused by the mosquito-borne malaria parasite.

clue.text: One thousand twins, to be blunt

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
twins are a pair

explanation.surface: Someone frankly admits a thousand sets of twins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be blunt' reads as frankly, but 'blunt' is a verb meaning to dull.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to weaken or dull, just as to blunt an edge or a feeling.

clue.text: Average knock-up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a rap is a knock

explanation.surface: A middling warm-up at tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock-up' suggests a practice game, but it is knock, RAP, read up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the normal or usual level, as in below par.

clue.text: Lining almost appears to go in the opposite direction

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped from the word for going backwards

parts.words: to go in the opposite direction
parts.note: to reverse is to go backwards

explanation.surface: A coat's lining almost seems to turn the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Revers are lapels turned back to show their lining or facing.

clue.text: Beware, lest this stone fall upon you, in the jungle!

definitions.text: Beware, lest this stone fall upon you, in the jungle!

parts.words: Beware, lest this stone fall upon you, in the jungle!
parts.note: a striped gem shares its name with the gaze of a big cat watching you in the forest

explanation.surface: A warning against being hit by a falling rock in the jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall upon' means a gaze falling on you, not a rock dropping; the striped stone is named after a big cat's look.
explanation.definitionFit: The banded brown quartz gemstone is named after the eye of the big striped cat.
